text:
5 Stunning Places Where You Can Stand Closer To Space Than Anywhere Else On Earth
Curated By :
Last Updated:
A trip here means not just exploring Earth’s natural beauty, but also standing, quite literally, closer to the stars than anywhere else on the planet.
1/6
Are you thinking Mount Everest is the closest spot on Earth to space? Think again. The real winner lies thousands of kilometres away—in Ecuador. One mountain here reaches closer to the stars than any other place on the planet. The reason has nothing to do with sea level—and everything to do with geometry. (Image-Canva)
2/6
Mount Chimborazo- In Ecuador, stands Mount Chimborazo, a dormant volcano about 6,263 metres high. Located just one degree south of the equator, its position gives it a unique edge. When measured from the planet’s core, Chimborazo’s summit lies 6,384.4 kilometres away, making it the farthest point from the centre of the Earth. (Image-Canva)
ADVERTISEMENT
3/6
Quito- Perched at 2,850 metres above sea level, Ecuador’s capital, Quito, almost seems to float among the clouds. Added proudly to the UNESCO World Heritage Site, it is a living museum of baroque churches, sunlit plazas, and winding, steep streets. While exploring Quito, check out the ornate La Compañía de Jesús Church, renowned for its gold-laden interiors. (Image-Canva)
4/6
The Amazon Rainforest: From the Andean highlands, descend into the lush depths of the Amazon Rainforest, one of the planet’s most biodiverse regions. Adventure seekers can head to Tena for white-water rafting and rainforest hikes. (Image-Canva)
ADVERTISEMENT
5/6
The Galápagos- Not a single trip to Ecuador is considered complete without exploring the legendary Galápagos Islands, the volcanic archipelago. Spend your mornings snorkelling with sea turtles and your afternoons walking lava trails beside giant tortoises. (Image-Canva)
